I am a 45-year-old farmer with 20 years on this land. I know my 58.1 mu in Quzhou well. My family has four people, so we have labor at home, but we cannot afford to hire many outside workers. I have a well for irrigation, which gives me control over water, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not waste a single drop.

My system is built around stevia. I have grown it for years and the buyers trust my product. I keep 25 mu for stevia because it is my best cash crop. I also need grain for the family and feed for our use, so 20 mu will stay in the wheat-maize double crop that never fails us. The remaining 13.1 mu I plant with cotton — it brings in good money and I understand its habits.

For the wheat already in the ground from last autumn: I will top-dress with urea when it greens up, irrigate at jointing and heading, and spray twice for aphids and disease if they show up. I use improved seed from the county co-op. I expect around 475 kg/mu this year.

For summer maize: As soon as the wheat is harvested in early June, I plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no-tillage. This saves time and keeps the soil moist. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress nitrogen at the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice if the summer turns dry. Expected yield is about 565 kg/mu.

For cotton: I plough deep in spring because cotton needs loose soil for its taproot. I plant hybrid Bt cotton seeds in late April. I apply basal fertilizer at planting and top-dress at flowering. I will irrigate three times during the boll-forming period. Even with Bt cotton, I watch closely and spray three times for pests if needed. I expect about 305 kg/mu of seed cotton.

For stevia: This is my main focus. In April, I rotary till between rows to kill weeds. I apply fertilizer in two splits — one when regrowth starts strong, and one before the first harvest. Stevia leaves need steady moisture, so I will irrigate five times through the season. I harvest twice, once in mid-summer and again in autumn before frost. Expected dried leaf yield is about 185 kg/mu.
